headline: State Park Capacity and Camping Reservations
reservation: General entry is managed at the gate and may be paused when parking lots reach capacity; no timed-entry is currently required. Camping at the park's single developed site requires booking through the Utah State Parks system up to four months in advance. Check the official park site for current day-use fees and any temporary closures of sensitive habitat areas.

days.title: Lava Tubes and Dunes

stops.name: Lava Flow Overlook
stops.detail: Traverse ancient basalt fields and peer into volcanic pits along this moderate trail.

stops.name: Petrified Dunes
stops.detail: Scramble across frozen waves of Navajo sandstone that offer elevated views of the canyon floor.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; traffic is light early in the morning
days.note: Bring a powerful light source if you intend to step inside the accessible lava tubes.

days.title: Canyon Walls and Narrow Slots

stops.name: Jenny's Canyon
stops.detail: Walk the short, sandy path to a narrow slot canyon and a scenic overlook of the southern park entrance.

stops.name: Hidden Pinyon Trail
stops.detail: Follow this interpretive loop to see desert flora and unique geological features tucked against the red cliffs.

days.driving: Local transfers under 15 minutes; conditions vary by park gate activity
days.note: Jenny's Canyon is closed annually from mid-March to June for raptor nesting.

days.title: White Rocks and High Overlooks

stops.name: White Rocks Amphitheater
stops.detail: Explore the northern end of the park where bright white sandstone mounds contrast with the lower red rocks.

stops.name: Snow Canyon Overlook
stops.detail: Drive to the Red Mountain trailhead off Highway 18, then hike to Snow Canyon Overlook; this is a 4.8-mile round-trip outing, not a roadside viewpoint.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes to reach northern trailheads; watch for cyclists
days.note: Allow time, water, and suitable footwear for the rocky and sandy 4.8-mile round-trip overlook hike; avoid scheduling it during intense summer heat.

intel.title: Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Lots at Jenny's Canyon and Sand Dunes are small and fill by 9 AM on spring weekends. Use the larger lot at the Upper Galoot area if others are full.

intel.title: Narrow Canyon Coverage
intel.text: Expect total signal loss within the lava tubes and Jenny's Canyon. Stronger signals are usually found at the White Rocks area near the northern boundary.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: No fuel or food is sold inside the park. Ivins is the final stop for water and snacks before entering the south gate.

intel.title: Summer Sun Strategy
intel.text: Midday temperatures on the black lava rocks can exceed 100 degrees. Limit hiking to the window between 6 AM and 10 AM during July and August.

intel.title: Pet Restrictions
intel.text: Pets are only permitted on the West Canyon Road and the Whiptail Trail. They are prohibited on all other desert trails to protect the fragile crust.

plan.arrival: Pick up a car at SGU and stock up on water in St. George before checking into a rental in Ivins, located just 5 minutes from the park gate.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for all paved park roads; RVs should check length limits for the campground stalls.
plan.goldenHour: The Sand Dunes area is the preferred sunset spot as the fading light intensifies the orange hue of the fine sand.
